plain_language_meaning: Terahertz radiation generally refers to electromagnetic radiation between the microwave and infrared regions of the spectrum.
safety_note: This term should not be used by itself to imply a medical effect or therapeutic outcome.
commercial_relevance: Helps explain what terahertz means in consumer wellness device descriptions.
notes: Use as a neutral spectrum-definition row.

plain_language_meaning: Terahertz is commonly discussed as a frequency band rather than as one single fixed frequency.
safety_note: Frequency-band language should remain educational and should not be converted into unsupported dose or protocol claims.
commercial_relevance: Helps users understand why vague terahertz claims can be difficult to compare.
notes: Avoid implying that all terahertz devices operate identically.

plain_language_meaning: Consumer terahertz devices may use terahertz-related language in different ways depending on design, emitter type, wavelength/frequency claims, heat output, and supporting light technologies.
safety_note: Consumers should review manufacturer instructions and avoid assuming that category language proves a specific biological result.
commercial_relevance: Supports clearer comparison between terahertz-labeled wellness devices.
notes: Useful for separating product-category language from evidence claims.

plain_language_meaning: Terahertz terminology can describe a physical category or claimed emission type, but that is separate from proving a medical claim.
safety_note: Do not treat terahertz labeling as evidence of diagnosis, treatment, cure, prevention, or disease-specific benefit.
commercial_relevance: Protects Holistix copy from overstating what the technology means.

plain_language_meaning: Terahertz radiation is generally discussed as part of the non-ionizing region of the electromagnetic spectrum.
safety_note: Non-ionizing does not automatically mean risk-free; intensity, heat, distance, exposure time, device design, and user condition still matter.
commercial_relevance: Helps users avoid the false shortcut that non-ionizing always equals harmless.

plain_language_meaning: Some devices associated with terahertz, infrared, or combined energy delivery may create warmth or thermal sensation.
safety_note: Users should avoid overheating, burns, prolonged exposure, use over numb skin, or use when heat sensitivity is impaired.
commercial_relevance: Important for products that combine terahertz claims with heat or infrared-style output.
notes: Safety row should appear clearly on the page.

plain_language_meaning: Distance can affect perceived intensity, warmth, and exposure characteristics for many light, heat, or energy-emitting devices.
safety_note: Follow manufacturer instructions. Do not create aggressive exposure routines from general online claims.
commercial_relevance: Useful for safe buyer education without giving a dosage protocol.

plain_language_meaning: Exposure time is a major variable in any consumer device that emits light, heat, or energy.
safety_note: This dataset does not provide dosage protocols. Users should follow device instructions and consult a qualified professional when appropriate.
commercial_relevance: Prevents users from interpreting the dataset as a treatment guide.
notes: No disease protocols or guaranteed outcomes.

plain_language_meaning: Some consumer products may combine terahertz-related positioning with infrared, blue light, red light, heat, massage, airflow, or other features.
safety_note: When multiple technologies are combined, claims should identify which feature is being discussed and avoid assigning all effects to terahertz alone.
commercial_relevance: Helpful for Holistix product education where devices may combine several feature categories.

plain_language_meaning: A useful terahertz device listing should separate claimed emission type, light source, heat output, power source, safety instructions, intended use, and disclaimers.
safety_note: If exact specifications are unavailable, copy should say so rather than imply precision.
commercial_relevance: Supports cleaner product-page and comparison-page language.
notes: Good row for future product-spec audits.

plain_language_meaning: Terahertz wellness devices should generally be described with cautious educational language because consumer-market claims can move faster than strong clinical evidence.
safety_note: Avoid broad statements that terahertz devices are proven to treat medical conditions.
commercial_relevance: Keeps the category useful without creating claim-risk landmines.

plain_language_meaning: This reference index is not a treatment protocol and does not recommend terahertz devices for any disease or condition.
safety_note: Users with medical conditions, implanted devices, pregnancy, heat sensitivity, neuropathy, or uncertain risk factors should consult a qualified healthcare professional before use.
commercial_relevance: Protects educational project boundaries and product compliance.

plain_language_meaning: Consumers can compare terahertz-labeled devices by reviewing claimed technology, supporting specifications, instructions, safety warnings, return policy, warranty, and whether claims are educational or medical.
safety_note: A checklist is not proof of safety or effectiveness; it is only a way to organize buyer questions.
commercial_relevance: Useful for searchers comparing Holistix against vague marketplace listings.
notes: Good content bridge to commercial pages without hard-selling.

plain_language_meaning: Educational descriptions should separate what a device is claimed to emit from what outcomes are clinically proven.
safety_note: Avoid borrowed authority, disease claims, guaranteed results, and unsupported before-and-after promises.
commercial_relevance: Useful for keeping Holistix data assets citation-worthy and less salesy.
notes: This is the Rockefeller firewall row: protect the asset.

plain_language_meaning: Terahertz consumer-device language should be reviewed periodically because terminology, evidence, and product claims can change.
safety_note: Rows should be updated when stronger evidence, clearer safety standards, or manufacturer specifications become available.
commercial_relevance: Supports version history, future audits, and AI-reference trust.
